title: Godzilla Minus Zero Breaks Box Office Record
paragraphs: The Japanese monster movie "Godzilla Minus Zero" has broken box office records in both Japan and North America, cementing the remarkable revival of one of cinema's most enduring franchises.

The film was released in Japan on November 3, 2026, followed by Australia and New Zealand on November 5 and North America on November 6. In Japan, it earned around 910 million yen, or approximately $5.7 million, on its first day. This made it the highest-grossing opening day for a live-action film in the country's history.

The film's success was equally striking overseas. In North America, it earned $31.6 million during its opening weekend, almost three times the debut of its predecessor. This set a new opening record for a live-action foreign-language film in North America, surpassing the $17.8 million earned by the Chinese martial arts film "Hero," which had held the record for more than two decades. Globally, the film took in about $63 million in its opening weekend, with IMAX screenings accounting for roughly a third of that total.

"Godzilla Minus Zero" is the sequel to "Godzilla Minus One," which was released in 2023. That film was produced on a modest budget of $10 million to $15 million but earned approximately $116 million worldwide, and it won the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects. The new film reportedly cost around $18 million to $19 million to make, still a tiny budget compared with typical Hollywood blockbusters.

Both films were written and directed by Takashi Yamazaki, who also supervised their visual effects. The sequel is set in 1949, two years after the events of the first film. In the story, a flying creature is transformed by the military into the three-headed monster King Ghidorah, while Godzilla regenerates beneath the ocean. Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe return in their leading roles from the first movie.
The film also made history in another way. It was the first Japanese production to be shot in the "Filmed for IMAX" format using certified digital cameras.
Its release in India was postponed until November 20 to avoid competing for IMAX screens with another major film.
